query.expected_observation: A complete, non-numerical-failure NMPC execution with publicly readable terminal_error_m, holding_max_error_m and holding_max_speed_m_s for candidate cb6db6..., typically terminal error near 0.003-0.006 m and holding error <=0.010 m, plus a measurable peak holding speed; if the speed-aware cost acts as intended the peak speed should fall below 0.0879 m/s, and a value at or below 0.020 m/s with holding error <=0.010 m would be a fresh complete final-fidelity pass to be read in full and selected immediately. Actual per-channel tension expenditure (unequal control effort) is to be reported from the measured trace.
query.fixed_conditions: Frozen task tasks/reach_hold_b3_050.json (task_identity 062de8ca2fd2acaebdbf856ba8fc3420d88c8d3943cfa789c5c9e6f06e486c6b): target [0.29,-0.035,0.19] m, zero initial state, 0.50 s duration, final window [0.45,0.50] s, position limit 0.010 m, speed limit 0.020 m/s, tension bounds [0,8] N, control period 0.01 s, physics timestep 0.0005 s; candidate cb6db6... (2 segments, 12 cells per segment, 4 tendons, 8 N channel bounds); frozen NMPC recipe horizon=10, substeps=1, replan_period_s=0.1, max_iterations<=120, tolerance=1e-6, holding/terminal tip-speed weights 0.1/0.1, tip_speed_scale 0.02; frozen evaluation profile ac83935...; no task relaxation, no acceptance or credit inherited from the historical M2 NMPC (0.003148372648914904 m / 0.006038027478928508 m / 0.11137394399884916 m/s) or the historical native-schedule replay (0.004515550349894086 m / 0.006675937086453473 m / 0.08788779126447174 m/s); structure 1 NMPC is used at most once here.
query.hypothesis: On the reference structure, one fresh closed-loop NMPC execution under this Study's frozen recipe (horizon 10, substeps 1, replan 0.1 s, max_iterations<=120, tolerance 1e-6, holding_tip_speed_weight=0.1, terminal_tip_speed_weight=0.1, tip_speed_scale=0.02, holding_speed_cost_mode=time_integral_v1, holding_brake_lead_s=0.0) will produce a complete measured 0.5 s reach whose final-window peak tip speed is lower than the historical same-structure values 0.1114 m/s (NMPC) and 0.0879 m/s (native schedule), because the frozen cost explicitly penalizes spatial tip speed at and after the settling-window start; if the residual ring is damped to amplitude <~1.4 mm the task can pass, otherwise the measured gap quantifies the braking deficit on this structure.
query.interpretation: This is a finite, fresh, independently measured local control test on the reference structure, not a convergence claim and not evidence of structural infeasibility. History records keep their original Study identity and give no execution, solve, success or SELECT credit; the purpose is new measured information under the current frozen profile (does the explicit holding/terminal tip-speed cost reduce final-window tip speed on this structure?), not a repeat to consume budget. If the result is a complete final-fidelity pass, the full new evaluation will be publicly read and selected with zero extra confirmations and the Study stopped; if not, the measured speed/error pair (with reported unequal channel expenditure, not attributed solely to structure) will decide between a braking-focused native control optimization of structure 1 seeded from the measured applied tensions and a legal second-structure modification.
query.stopping_condition: Stop this action when the single NMPC execution returns a saved complete result or a numerical failure. Then publicly read its L1 result and full evaluation data once; on a fresh complete final-fidelity pass of the frozen task, record SELECT for that exact execution and stop the Study. On a non-pass, record the measured terminal/holding error and peak holding speed, do not repeat structure-1 NMPC, and choose the next action under remaining caps (provider ~38 after this action, NMPC 1 of 2, mathematical 26, physical launches 3 of 4, native optimizations 2 unspent).
query.weakening_observation: Any of: execution aborts with numerical failure or >=3 unusable updates so no complete task evaluation exists; OR holding_max_speed_m_s >= 0.1114 m/s, i.e. the speed-aware frozen cost does not improve on history; OR holding_max_error_m > 0.010 m; OR position and speed both remain near-limit/marginal in a way consistent with an uncontrolled ~5-6 mm residual mode ring (amplitude ~ v/omega) rather than a control deficiency, which would weaken the hypothesis that fixed-structure closed-loop control can reach 0.020 m/s and would shift the next action toward a second, softer/legally modified structure.

query.hypothesis: The dominant holding_speed failure on the reference structure is an under-braked, late final approach, not an undamped residual mode: the measured peak speed occurs at 0.48 s (0.1114 m/s) and decays to 0.0232 m/s by 0.50 s (approx. 12 ms envelope), while position stays within 3.1-6.0 mm. Therefore starting the holding-speed cost ~0.06 s before the 0.45 s window with the maximum authorized family control weights (holding_tip_speed_weight=1.0, terminal_tip_speed_weight=1.0, vs 0.1/0.1) should shift arrival/crossing earlier so the transient is already decayed when the window opens. query.interpretation: This action is a design modification whose purpose is to open the one remaining NMPC slot on a fresh but nearly-equivalent structure, so that the speed-focused control recipe (weights 0.1 -> 1.0 plus holding_brake_lead_s=0.06) can be physically tested. query.expected_observation: research_analysis(mujoco_direct_control_v1, model_source=mujoco) admits and returns a bounded-sequence optimization result bound to candidate e85fc8 whose source is the legal unmeasured schedule e3a06aa1: sampled native proxy metrics covering indices 45-50 show holding max speed reduced well below 0.018 m/s (from the schedule's open-loop baseline) with holding max position error still <= 0.009 m, every sampled tension inside [0,8] N, all offsets within the declared coefficient limit, and a returned explicit full 50-interval schedule reference for later physical_replay.
query.fixed_conditions: Frozen task tasks/reach_hold_b3_050.json unmodified: target [0.29,-0.035,0.19] m, zero initial state, 0.50 s, hold window [0.45,0.50] s, position <= 0.010 m, speed <= 0.020 m/s, tension [0,8] N, control period 0.01 s, physics 0.0005 s. Candidate e85fc8 and its frozen structure/recipe unmodified (no generation, no structural edit, no new candidate). Single source: e3a06aa1 (exact open-loop ZOH schedule of actually applied NMPC tensions, unmeasured, no inherited acceptance, no channel_map). Native method mujoco_direct_control_v1 with local_control_search_v2: correction_window_s [0.26,0.50], knots_s [0.26,0.36,0.44,0.50] (4 = cap), iterations 3 (= cap), evaluation_requests 24 (= cap), coefficient_limit_n 2.0, difference_step_n 0.02, initial_radius_n 0.2, minimum_radius_n 1e-4, safety_margin_fraction 0.1 (local-model target margin only; acceptance unchanged), frozen task-local-v2 protocol passed verbatim. No NMPC (0 slots), no control_search, no RL, no new structure, no T1/T2 in this action.
query.hypothesis: The measured applied NMPC schedule on candidate e85fc8 misses only the holding-speed bound (0.04301 m/s vs 0.020, normalized excess 1.1505) with violations localized to the final samples driven by downward tip motion (vz = -0.03960 m/s at 0.49 s, -0.03515 m/s at 0.50 s) while holding position (0.004033 m) and terminal error (0.004033 m) are comfortably inside 0.010 m and peak applied tension is only 4.99 N of the 8 N bound. Therefore a bounded 4-knot tension-offset sequence applied to that exact legal schedule inside a late correction window (0.26-0.50 s) should be able to arrest the tip so that cloned native MuJoCo rollouts covering every holding sample show holding speed <= 0.018 m/s and holding position <= 0.009 m, yielding a legal explicit full schedule worth one independent full replay.
query.interpretation: This is a finite local bounded-sequence control search on one already physically evaluated structure using a native MuJoCo rollout proxy; it yields no task acceptance, no global feasibility claim, no physical gain and no model-fidelity claim. Its only output of value is an explicit in-bounds schedule plus local proxy evidence for whether a single independent replay is worth spending. Because e85fc8 pairs a legal FamilySpace change with a different (speed-aware) recipe, any residual advantage over the reference structure cannot be attributed to structure alone; actual unequal control expenditure must be reported.
query.stopping_condition: Stop this action when the single native optimization returns (or is rejected). If its own proxy shows holding speed <= 0.018 m/s and holding position <= 0.009 m with in-bounds tensions, proceed to exactly one independent full physical replay of that returned schedule on e85fc8; otherwise spend no replay on it and either use the one remaining study-wide native optimization on the other already-evaluated structure or close the Study with a legal STOP citing all_fresh_results. Native integration steps this action must stay <= 60000 (expected ~2.4e4).
query.weakening_observation: Admission rejected (source/settings/protocol/limit mismatch); or the search terminates with proxy holding speed still above 0.020 m/s (window braking authority insufficient at <=2.0 N coefficient limit); or speed improves only by pushing proxy holding position past 0.009 m / terminal error near 0.010 m; or the response search exhausts its 24 evaluation_requests / 3 iterations without measurable improvement over the source baseline; or the returned schedule violates [0,8] N bounds or is not a complete explicit 50-interval schedule. Any of these makes a full replay unsupported.

query.expected_observation: The native mujoco_direct_control_v1 response search completes within 24 evaluation requests and 3 iterations and returns a feasible predicted correction: every original normalized bound satisfied with the 5% margin (predicted holding_window max tip speed comfortably below 0.019 m/s, predicted holding position error at or below ~0.008 m, tensions inside [0,8] N), knot offsets within +/-2.0 N of the e3a06aa1 schedule, a reported predicted-vs-start speed reduction consistent with the ~0.023 m/s velocity increment needed over the last 0.06-0.10 s, and a legal candidate-bound 50-interval 0.01 s explicit schedule usable as an unmeasured replay source. No task relaxation, no structure change, no NMPC solve.
query.fixed_conditions: Frozen task tasks/reach_hold_b3_050.json: target [0.29,-0.035,0.19] m, zero initial state, 0.50 s duration, final [0.45,0.50] s hold, position <=0.010 m, speed <=0.020 m/s, tension [0,8] N, control 0.01 s, physics 0.0005 s; task and acceptance not relaxed. Candidate e85fc8 structure and stored speed-aware recipe unchanged (no FamilySpace edit, no new structure). Correction source is exactly the existing measured open-loop schedule e3a06aa1 (50 intervals, tendon_0..tendon_3). Native model is the candidate's own MuJoCo model on the task 0.01 s grid, prefix reconstructed from the frozen standardized initial pretension. Method limits respected: evaluation_requests=24, iterations=3, knots_s=[0.42,0.50] (2 knots), total native integration including prefix well under 60000 steps.
query.hypothesis: On frozen candidate e85fc8 the residual task failure of the measured closed-loop NMPC run 629f68a is localized to the final holding window: speed 0.04300968 m/s versus the 0.020 m/s limit at t=0.49 s, dominated by vertical velocity v_z=-0.03960 m/s, while holding position error is only 0.00403 m against the 0.010 m limit. That leaves about 6 mm of unused position headroom that can be spent on braking. Therefore a bounded local native-MuJoCo direct correction of the exact measured open-loop schedule e3a06aa1 (per-tendon tension offsets at knots 0.42 s and 0.50 s inside the correction window [0.40,0.50] s, coefficient limit 2.0 N, 5% margin inside every original task norm bound) can remove the predicted holding-speed excess without driving position error to 0.010 m, producing a new candidate-bound explicit schedule worth exactly one independent physical replay.
query.interpretation: This is one bounded, falsifiable local control experiment on a frozen structure: a native-model braking correction of an already-measured schedule in the last 0.10 s. Its predicted margins are a hypothesis to be tested in independent physics, not a physical gain. A positive predicted outcome would justify at most one independent replay; a negative outcome would leave e85fc8 with a measured speed-failure record and would not support any claim of convergence, model fidelity, or global/structural infeasibility. Actual, unequal control expenditure between the measured NMPC run and any corrected open-loop schedule must be reported as a control-effort difference and must not be attributed solely to structure.
query.stopping_condition: Execute this single native direct control optimization and read its result. If it returns a feasible predicted correction with all original bounds satisfied inside the 5% margin, next obtain the exact candidate-bound schedule it produced, spend exactly one of the two remaining independent physical launches replaying that exact legal source at full task fidelity, and if that replay is a fresh complete final-fidelity pass, publicly read the full new evaluation and immediately SELECT that exact candidate/control/result with zero extra confirmations, then stop. If the native analysis is infeasible, nonconvergent or limit-bound, record it as finite local numerical information, do not repeat the same-structure optimization without new information, and proceed to a legal STOP that publicly reads and cites all_fresh_results. No task relaxation, no third structure, no NMPC (budget 0).
query.weakening_observation: The native search returns no improving feasible correction, stays infeasible after the final iteration, terminates on the evaluation/iteration limits with the predicted holding-speed excess still positive, requires offsets beyond 2.0 N or tensions outside [0,8] N, or trades the speed violation for a predicted holding position error approaching or exceeding 0.010 m (i.e. the position headroom is smaller than assumed). Any of these is finite local numerical information about this window/knob set only, not evidence of structural or global infeasibility.

If predicted metrics still violate the 0.020 m/s speed bound, do NOT spend a physical launch; either use the remaining second Study-wide native optimization on the reference structure cb6db6 only if it retains decision relevance, or read /all_fresh_results and STOP citing all new results. query.hypothesis: On candidate e85fc8 the complete measured open-loop schedule e3a06aa1 fails only holding speed (0.043010 m/s at t=0.49 s vs 0.020 m/s limit, normalized excess 1.1505) while holding position is 0.004033 m with roughly 0.006 m unspent against the 0.010 m limit, and the violating sample is dominated by downward tip velocity (v_z = -0.039605 m/s, v_x = 0.016286 m/s). A bounded six-coefficient tension-offset correction added to that same measured schedule, ramping from 0 at t=0 to loaded channels 1/2 at 0.30 s and full four-channel authority at 0.50 s, offsets capped at 1.5 N inside the frozen [0,8] N channel bounds, yields a legal 50-interval schedule whose native MuJoCo prediction reaches holding-window peak speed below 0.020 m/s while predicted holding position stays below 0.010 m.

query.weakening_observation: Admission rejection; or the search stops with zero or one completed response step and returns no reduced schedule; or its best predicted schedule keeps holding peak speed above 0.020 m/s, or reaches it only with predicted holding position above 0.010 m, or only with every active offset pressed at the 1.5 N cap (cap binding); or the returned schedule is not a legal bounded 50-interval ZOH schedule. decision.selected_method: mujoco_direct_control_v1

query.expected_observation: The native MuJoCo direct control optimization returns within its declared limits (<=24 evaluation_requests, <=3 iterations, 4 knots, ~24,000 native integration steps <= 60,000) with a lower native objective than the seed schedule, a predicted holding-window max tip speed moved toward and ideally at or below 0.018 m/s, predicted terminal and holding position error <= 0.008 m, coefficient offsets strictly inside the +/-2 N limit, and every applied tension inside [0, 8] N. The returned schedule stays bound to candidate e85fc8 with the frozen task identity, and carries no inherited physical acceptance (task_acceptance=unmeasured).
query.fixed_conditions: Frozen task tasks/reach_hold_b3_050.json unchanged: target [0.29,-0.035,0.19] m, zero initial state, duration 0.50 s, holding window [0.45,0.50] s, position limit 0.010 m, speed limit 0.020 m/s, tension [0,8] N, control period 0.01 s, physics timestep 0.0005 s; frozen analysis_protocol passed verbatim (protocol_id task-local-v2, samples_s [0.0,0.1,0.3,0.45,0.49], windows_s [0.05,0.1,0.5]). Candidate e85fc8 design/geometry/material/route and its stored recipe are NOT modified; this action touches only the open-loop input schedule for MuJoCo-direct local search. model_source=mujoco, operating_point=standardized_initial_pretension (frozen t=0 initializer state; no prefix reconstruction), control_optimization.source=e3a06aa1 (candidate-bound complete explicit schedule, exact measured applied 629f68 tensions, correct interval count and tendon_order, no channel_map), settings version=local_control_search_v2, method=response, correction_window_s=[0.0,0.5] covering every required sample, knots_s=[0.0,0.30,0.40,0.50], active_coefficients=[8..15] (knot 0 and knot 1 offsets forced exactly zero so 0-0.30 s input is unchanged), coefficient_limit_n=2.0, initial_radius_n=0.5, minimum_radius_n=1e-4, difference_step_n=0.01, safety_margin_fraction=0.0 (legacy target; any margin is imposed by my own decision rule on the returned prediction, not by changing the bound). No NMPC (Study cap exhausted), no PPO, no structural edit, no new candidate, no physical launch in this action. Cross-structure control expenditure remains unequal and is not attributed to structure alone.
query.hypothesis: On candidate e85fc8, the exact measured NMPC applied-tension schedule (e3a06aa1 = 629f68 applied SI tensions, 51 ZOH samples, 0-0.5 s) already passes terminal and holding POSITION with margin (0.00403 m vs 0.010 m) and fails only holding SPEED (0.04301 vs 0.020 m/s), where the residual is a small downward tip drift (-0.0396 m/s in z at 0.49 s, -0.0352 m/s at 0.50 s). Because the last-window tensions are small (0.54-5.0 N, far below the 8 N bound and near-zero on tendon_0), there is unused actuation headroom. Therefore a bounded additive tension correction that ramps from zero at t=0.30 s to free knot offsets at t=0.40 s and t=0.50 s (8 active knot-major coefficients, |offset| <= 2 N) should lower the native MuJoCo predicted holding-window max tip speed while keeping terminal and holding position error small, because the failure is a late braking deficit along the final 0.2 s rather than a position-tracking failure.
query.interpretation: This is a bounded local, finite-parameter control correction on one structure and one starting schedule, evaluated in the native MuJoCo model. Any objective decrease is local numerical information near the evaluated coefficients; it is not convergence, not global or structural feasibility, and not evidence of model error, since no verified model-error bound exists and candidate/state/input/sampling alignment cannot be extended across structures. Because the seed schedule comes from a completed but non-accepted physical execution, no physical acceptance is inherited: the returned open-loop schedule is task_acceptance=unmeasured and only a fresh independent replay can establish an outcome.
query.stopping_condition: Execute exactly one native control optimization (native optimization 1 of 2 Study-wide, charged as 1 of 26 remaining mathematical evaluations; ~24,000 of 60,000 native steps; physical launches unchanged at 2 remaining, and only e85fc8's single full replay is conceivable later). Stop the search route after this single call returns or is refused - no repeat same-structure native optimization. If the returned schedule is native-predicted with holding-window max speed <= 0.018 m/s, position error <= 0.008 m and tensions within [0,8] N, then spend e85fc8's one full independent physical replay on that exact returned schedule, publicly read the fresh complete evaluation, and SELECT immediately at the first pass with zero extra confirmations. Otherwise go directly to a legal STOP that publicly reads and cites all_fresh_results (65130099, 629f68) plus every new result, and states that the improvement (if any) is finite local control improvement, not convergence, not model fidelity and not structural infeasibility.
query.weakening_observation: No decrease in the native objective after the first response iteration; offsets pinned at the +/-2 N coefficient limit; predicted holding speed still above 0.020 m/s; predicted terminal or holding position error above 0.009 m; a reported infeasible/ill-conditioned local model, unusable difference steps, or a solver error; or native steps exceeding the 60,000 Study allowance. Any of these means the late-window correction route is weak on this structure and the remaining independent replay is not spent on it. A native prediction only at the 0.020 s boundary (i.e. > 0.018 m/s) also counts as insufficient, since native prediction is not acceptance.
